subject.title: Control UI fails to load on Firefox desktop behind reverse proxy — CSP blocks Vite runtime eval(), 'Control UI did not start', WebSocket 1006

question: Should maintainers keep strict Control UI CSP and require live Firefox reverse-proxy proof before any WebSocket/auth behavior change, or consolidate this report into the older CSP/Zod issue?
rationale: The source-proven CSP/Zod portion overlaps an existing issue, but adding unsafe-eval would weaken the Control UI security boundary and the reported reverse-proxy WebSocket 1006 path has not been live-reproduced on current main.

options.title: Preserve CSP And Prove Proxy Path
options.body: Keep this issue open for live Firefox reverse-proxy proof while fixing the Zod/no-eval path under the overlapping CSP work.

options.title: Consolidate Into CSP Issue
options.body: Treat the WebSocket failure as likely startup fallout and move remaining discussion to the existing Control UI CSP/Zod issue.

options.title: Accept Unsafe Eval
options.body: Allow unsafe-eval in the Control UI CSP as a deliberate security tradeoff to unblock the reported startup failure.

recommendation.title: Preserve CSP And Prove Proxy Path
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for live Firefox reverse-proxy proof while fixing the Zod/no-eval path under the overlapping CSP work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest feature-history trail for the Control UI bootstrap/CSP security boundary.
